problem_summary.summary: Return the greatest sum of any non-empty path, where a path may start and end at any nodes but cannot branch.
problem_summary.input_output: Input: a non-empty binary-tree root. Return the maximum path sum as an integer.

brute_force.explanation: For every node as a possible path apex, independently search its left and right descendant trees for their greatest downward sums; combine positive branches with the apex.
brute_force.correctness_idea: Every simple path has a unique highest node (its apex). At that apex the path consists of at most one downward chain in each child subtree, so evaluating the best such pair considers every path.
brute_force.time_complexity: O(n^2) worst case because a descendant search is repeated for each possible apex.
brute_force.space_complexity: O(n) auxiliary for the node list and traversal stacks.

optimized.explanation: Process nodes bottom-up without recursion. For each node, store the best downward gain from that node; update the global answer with the node plus positive gains from both children.
optimized.correctness_idea: A parent can use only one child branch as a downward continuation, so each node returns its value plus the larger nonnegative child gain. A complete path may join both child gains at that node, which is considered for the global maximum.
optimized.time_complexity: O(n) — each node is placed in the traversal order once and processed once in reverse.
optimized.space_complexity: O(n) auxiliary for the order list, gain map, and traversal stack; avoids call-stack overflow on a skewed tree.

steps.event: Process leaf 7 in reverse traversal order.
steps.action: Store downward gain 7; global best becomes 7.
Update best to 10; return downward gain 2 + max(7,1) = 9.

steps.condition: Negative child gains are clamped to zero before extending a path.
steps.action: Neither node improves the best path; retain 10.

edge_cases.handling: The answer starts at the smallest integer and each node is considered as a non-empty path.
Its value is the only possible path sum.

edge_cases.case: A child subtree has negative gain
edge_cases.handling: The gain is ignored when extending or joining a path.
